claims.text: The initial NbTaTiV or similar refractory high-entropy alloy is a homogeneous single-phase solid solution.
The as-cast initial alloy contains minimal intrinsic nano-precipitates.
Heat treatment can cause an initially single-phase refractory high-entropy alloy to form precipitates.
The proposed heat treatment will produce a controlled distribution of nanoscale precipitates.
Precipitate-forming heat treatment will leave the overall alloy composition unchanged.
Nano-precipitates impede dislocation motion by serving as pinning points.
Precipitate-mediated inhibition of dislocation motion increases elevated-temperature yield strength.
Precipitate-induced changes in local lattice distortion cause measurable shifts in elastic moduli.
The heat-treated alloy will have higher yield strength than the baseline alloy between 873 K and 1073 K.
The heat-treated alloy will exhibit modified, potentially increased, elevated-temperature elastic stiffness relative to the baseline.
Precipitate pinning will reduce the temperature-dependent softening rate of yield strength.
Single-phase refractory high-entropy alloys can retain high yield strength and substantial softening resistance at elevated temperatures.
NbTaTiV exhibits temperature-dependent elastic anisotropy at elevated temperatures, and its elastic moduli can be determined by in situ neutron diffraction and resonant ultrasound spectroscopy.
TEM and XRD can quantify the size and density of the proposed nano-precipitates.
Grain boundaries and other microstructural features may affect the magnitude of the precipitate-related response.

contradictions.description: The baseline is alternately described as 'as-cast' and 'as-cast, homogenized.' Homogenization is a post-casting heat treatment, so the actual baseline processing state is ambiguous and may not be equivalent to a genuinely as-cast state.
